speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To better understand your sudden-onset lower back pain radiating down your leg, can you tell me how long this pain has been present and on what side of your body you feel the radiation?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a classic presentation of sciatica, likely from a disc herniation. Can you tell me if you have any numbness, tingling, or weakness in that leg, and does the pain worsen when you cough or sneeze? Also, what is your favorite position to lie in for relief?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sharp lower back pain radiating to the leg and foot. I also have Pain worsens with movement, The onset of pain while exercising.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: MRI Lumbar Spine to visualize potential disc herniation.
REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide any available X-rays or prior MRI scans of the lumbar region if they exist.
Has the pain reached a severity of 7 or higher on a scale of 10, and do you experience any loss of bladder or bowel control?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Lumbar_Spine: Evidence of L5-S1 disc herniation impinging on the adjacent nerve root. No prior X-rays or MRI scans available in the current data. Pain severity not recorded in the provided dataset; bladder or bowel control status not recorded in the provided dataset.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: L5-S1 Disc Herniation with Sciatica. The MRI confirms the L5-S1 disc is herniating and compressing the nerve root, which explains your sharp pain radiating to your foot that started during exercise. I recommend immediate rest, avoiding heavy lifting, and starting anti-inflammatory medication; if you have any new trouble with your bladder or bowel, seek emergency care immediately.
